highlights.description: The `academyos` command line: keep a course as a course-spec directory in git, then check it, push it with its slide decks, translations, quizzes and recorded narration, pull the academy's copy back, and publish it
The Go SDK, `github.com/academyosio/academyos-go/academyos`: an API client with typed errors for the public AcademyOS API, and `coursepkg` for course-spec directories

added.description: `academyos whoami`: the key's principal, academy and scopes
`academyos course validate`: check a course directory, exiting 2 on errors
`academyos course push`: validate, upload only the files the academy lacks, apply the course, and record the academy's IDs in the directory; `--dry-run` reports what would change
`academyos course publish`: publish a pushed course

`academyos course pull`: write the academy's copy of a course, as last pushed, into its directory, or into an empty one with `--course`; `--dry-run` lists the changes and `--force` overwrites local changes
`academyos pronunciations push` and `get`: replace and print an academy's pronunciations, with a diff and `--dry-run`
`academyos version`, reporting the module version it was built from

`academyos` package: `New` with `Options` (API key, URL), typed API errors, course push, publish and pull, pronunciations, and lower-level calls; plain http is allowed only to `localhost`, `.localhost` names and loopback addresses
`coursepkg`: the files a course-spec directory needs, including each deck's recorded narration in `recordings/`
The public AcademyOS API's OpenAPI document, in `openapi/`

tests.description: The client, course packages, push, pull into empty and git-tracked directories, pronunciation diffs and dry runs, and the CLI; every client request is checked against the public API document

documentation.description: A documentation site with getting started, command line, Go SDK and AI agent guides, and the API reference rendered with Scalar
INIT-ACADEMYOSGO-001 requirements, design, plan and roadmap

infrastructure.description: CI tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, lints, and builds the docs site
